[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [scripture] "Psalm 19:8-9 (20:7-8)" vs "Ψευδὴς ἵππος εἰς σωτηρίαν...Οὗτοι ἐν ἅρμασι καὶ ἵποις": Wrong psalm citation: these verses are Psalm 32:17 and 33:17 LXX (Hebrew 33:17 and 20:7-8), not Psalm 19:8-9.; [agency] "The same thing as the hobbling and the fall is indicated here" vs "ταὐτὸν δὲ τῷ συμποδισμῷ καὶ τῇ πτώσει διὰ τῆς καταφορᾶς καὶ καρώσεως ἐνταῦθα δεδήλωται": Passive 'is indicated' obscures that subject is the preceding scriptural words; 'the same thing' refers to what was shown, not what 'is indicated' as equivalent.; [completeness] "a remnant of wrath girded on" vs "λείψανον θυμοῦ περιζωσθέν": Missing 'you' or 'itself' as object of girding; ambiguous whether remnant girds itself or is girded by God.; [modality] "is subject to confession and changes of mind" vs "ἐξομολόγησιν ὑπόκειται καὶ μεταγνώσεσιν": 'Subject to' weakens the Greek; ὑπόκειται means 'lies under/undergoes/is liable to' confession and repentances as consequences. | part 2/5: [scripture] "Psalm 82 (83)" vs "τοῦ ΠΒ": ΠΒ = 82 in Greek numerals, but Hebrew/English is 83; bracket should be (83) not (83) — actually this is correct. Wait: ΠΒ = 80+2 = 82 LXX = 83 Hebrew. The English says 'Psalm 82 (83)' which is correct. No defect.; [scripture] "Psalm 72 (73)" vs "τῷ ΟΒ": ΟΒ = 70+2 = 72 LXX = 73 Hebrew. The English says 'Psalm 72 (73)' which is correct. No defect.; [agency] "he first gives thanks to God who received his supplications" vs "χάριν πρῶτον ὁμολογεῖ τῷ τὰς ἱκετείας δεξαμένῳ θεῷ": 'his supplications' implies the psalmist's, but Greek τὰς ἱκετείας is simply 'the supplications' with no possessive; could be general or the people's; [completeness] "having spoken piously in Psalm 72 (73)" vs "κἂν τῷ ΟΒ προευφημήσας εὐσεβῶς": κἂν = 'even if' or 'also' is untranslated; 'having spoken piously' misses that προευφημήσας means 'having spoken well beforehand/praised in advance', not just 'spoken piously' — but this is near-synonym territory; [modality] "unless someone remembers" vs "εἰ μὴ τῶν προτέρων τις μνημονεύσας": εἰ μὴ with participle = 'if not... someone having remembered', but the construction with participle is conditional; 'unless someone remembers' captures the sense adequately; [agency] "the nation has been despised" vs "τὸ ἔθνος ὑπερῶπται": ὑπερῶπται is perfect passive 'has been despised/looked down upon'; English is correct | part 3/5: [agency] "a turbulent struggle gripped the depths" vs "τὰς ἀβύσσους εἶχεν ἀγὼν ταραχώδης": Subject is 'struggle' (ἀγὼν), not external agent; 'gripped' misrepresents εἶχεν 'had'; [completeness] "the arrows from heaven were hurled down" vs "τὰ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ βέλη κατεφέρετο": βέλη means 'missiles/projectiles', not specifically 'arrows'; [agency] "lightning flashed across the inhabited world and shook the earth with an earthquake" vs "ἀστραπαὶ τὴν οἰκουμένην κατηύγαζον καὶ σεισμὸν ἀνεκίνει τὴν γῆν": σεισμὸν 'earthquake' is subject of ἀνεκίνει 'was moving', not lightning; lightning illuminates, earthquake moves earth; [completeness] "the waters of the Red Sea gave way" vs "τῆς ἐρυθρᾶς θαλάσσης εἷξεν ὕδατα": ὕδατα is subject 'waters yielded', not 'waters of the Red Sea gave way' as if sea yielded; [modality] "as if shrinking back in fear" vs "καθάπερ εἰ φόβῳ τινὶ συστελλόμενα": συστελλόμενα is middle/passive 'contracting/drawing together', not active 'shrinking back'; [completeness] "Thunder crashed in the sky" vs "βρονταὶ δὲ ἐρράγησαν ἐν αἰθέρι": ἐρράγησαν means 'burst/broke forth', not merely 'crashed'; stronger rupture image | part 4/5: [agency] "another passage says it was when he bound" vs "ἄλλος μέν φησιν ἡνίκα Συνέδησεν": ἄλλος is 'another' person/author, not 'another passage'; subject of Συνέδησεν is God, not 'it'; [completeness] "He presents to us the circle of the sky" vs "Κύκλον ἡμῖν αἰθέριον ὑποβάλλει": Dropped 'ethereal/aetherial' (αἰθέριον); renders only 'circle of the sky'; [negation] "is not to be found in the divine oracles, so that we should not imagine" vs "οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν τοῖς θείοις λογίοις εὑρεῖν, ἵν'... ἐννοήσωμεν": Greek says 'not found... so that we might imagine' (positive purpose), English flips to 'so that we should not imagine' (negative); [completeness] "For the divine Scriptures present water under the earth, not heaven" vs "ὕδωρ γὰρ ὑπὸ γῆν, οὐκ οὐρανόν, αἱ θεῖαι γραφαὶ παριστᾶσι": Greek word order emphasizes 'water under earth, not heaven'; English obscures this is direct contrast to 'heaven' as what is NOT under earth; [completeness] "and waters above the heaven set as a boundary" vs "καὶ ὑπὲρ οὐρανὸν δὲ ὕδατα τέλους δίκην ὑποκείμεναι": Dropped 'moreover' (δὲ); 'set as a boundary' weakens τέλους δίκην ὑποκείμεναι 'lying-under as limit/end'; [scripture] "(Psalm 104:2)" vs "Ἐκτείνων γάρ φησι τὸν οὐρανὸν ὡσεὶ δέρριν ὁ στεγάζων ἐν ὕδασι τὰ ὑπερῷα αὐτοῦ": Verse is Psalm 103:2 in LXX numbering, not 104:2; English gives Hebrew/English numbering only, no LXX number; [completeness] "And the sun is said to run" vs "ἀπ' ἄκρου τε εἰς ἄκρον ἥλιον διαθεῖν... λέγεται": Dropped 'from end to end' (ἀπ' ἄκρου τε εἰς ἄκρον) in this clause, though appears later; [completeness] "And he says, "He established the heaven"" vs "καὶ Ὁ στήσας φησὶν οὐρανόν": Dropped 'the one having established' as substantive participle; 'He established' makes it finite verb; [completeness] "(not "he who leads it around in a circle")" vs "οὐχ ὁ κύκλῳ περιάγων αὐτόν": Dropped 'in circle' (κύκλῳ) as adverbial; 'in a circle' is weaker than 'in circle' as dative of manner; [completeness] "(not "to be whirled around like a circle")" vs "οὐχ ὡς κύκλον περιελίττεσθαι": Greek has infinitive 'to be whirled around' but English adds 'like' not in source (ὡς = 'as', already in positive clause) | part 5/5: [source_identity] "He says that the divine way has no visible trace" vs "Τὴν θείαν ὁδὸν λέγει μηδὲν ἴχνος ἔχειν θεωρητὸν": Subject is ambiguous/impersonal 'he says,' not 'He [God] says'; 'θεωρητὸν' means 'visible/observable,' not 'visible trace'; [completeness] "unlike the human way" vs "ὥσπερ τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην": Dropped 'ὥσπερ' = 'just as,' not 'unlike'; meaning reversed: 'as the human [way does]'; [negation] "not even the paths of a ship sailing the sea can be recognized" vs "μηδὲ τρίβους νηὸς ποντοπορούσης ὁ Σολομὼν ἐπιγινώσκεσθαι λέγει": μηδὲ = 'not even' is correct but context is positive: Solomon says paths are NOT recognized; English 'can be recognized' obscures that Solomon states they are unrecognizable; [modality] "it is no longer a journey of movement for God" vs "οὐκέτι πορεία τις θεῷ μεταβατική": μεταβατική = 'of change/transition,' i.e. local motion; 'for God' = dative of possession/reference, not 'for God's benefit'; [agency] "so that he might lead them through it" vs "ἵνα καὶ διὰ ταύτης αὐτοῖς καθηγήσαιτο": Subject is God implied, but 'he' ambiguous; καθηγήσαιτο = 'he might lead/guide,' correct; [completeness] "the stretch of the Red Sea was brief for them in their journey" vs "βραχὺ μὲν αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἐρυθρᾶς ἐγένετο κατὰ τὴν πορείαν": τὸ τῆς ἐρυθρᾶς = 'the [part] of the Red [Sea],' correct; but 'μὲν' sets up contrast with 'δὲ' later, partly lost; [completeness] "while the stretch through the land was long and lengthy" vs "πολὺ δὲ καὶ πολυχρόνιον τὸ διὰ γῆς": πολυχρόνιον = 'lengthy in time,' 'long-lasting,' not just 'lengthy'; temporal duration emphasized; [scripture] "Psalm 76:21 (77:20)" vs "Ὡδήγησας ὡς πρόβατα τὸν λαόν σου ἐν χειρὶ Μωυσῆ καὶ Ἀαρών": LXX Ps 76:21 = Heb Ps 77:20, correct

ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'Some trust in chariots … we rose and stood upright' is LXX Ps 19:8-9 (Eng 20:7-8), correctly cited; 'A horse is a false hope' (Ps 32:17) is quoted alongside it. Ps 82 (83) and 72 (73) are correct. 'Is not to be found in the divine oracles, so that we should not imagine a wheel-like circuit' gives the sense of οὐκ ἔστιν … εὑρεῖν, ἵν' … ἐννοήσωμεν, where the negation of the main clause governs the result clause: Scripture gives no ground for imagining it. 'Unlike the human way' renders the elliptical ὥσπερ τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην ('as the human way [has]'). Psalm 104:2 is the English number for LXX 103:2. 'Another passage' for ἄλλος, 'arrows' for βέλη, 'crashed' for ἐρράγησαν and the like are idiomatic.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I found no meaning error. Οὗτοι ἐν ἅρμασι καὶ οὗτοι ἐν ἵπποις … αὐτοὶ συνεποδίσθησαν καὶ ἔπεσαν is LXX Ps 19:8-9 (Eng 20:7-8), so the reference is correct; Ps 75 is only the lemma under discussion. ὁμολογεῖ χάριν means 'acknowledges a favour, gives thanks', so 'gives thanks' is right.
